walkthroughs.body_html:
The Cold War in Asia 1945-93 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Cold War in Asia 1945-93 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Cold War in Asia 1945-93.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who delivered the Iron Curtain speech?
options: Truman
Churchill
Attlee
Marshall
Warsaw
Gdansk
Krakow
Prague
The Truman Doctrine ordered the dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan.
Ideological incompatibility plus mutual suspicion after WWII — disputes over Eastern Europe, the atomic bomb, and broken wartime agreements.
Stalin started it by invading Eastern Europe after the war.
It began when the USSR shot down a US spy plane.

mcqs.q: How was the Cuban Missile Crisis resolved?
options: It began when the USSR shot down a US spy plane.
A secret deal: the USSR withdrew missiles from Cuba; the US publicly pledged not to invade Cuba and secretly agreed to remove Jupiter missiles from Turkey.
The crisis ended when Castro persuaded Khrushchev to withdraw.
Kennedy stared Khrushchev down and the Soviets backed off unconditionally.

mcqs.q: What did the Truman Doctrine commit the US to in 1947?
options: It began when the USSR shot down a US spy plane.
Supporting free peoples resisting communist takeover — initially Greece and Turkey — formalising the policy of containment articulated by George Kennan.
The Truman Doctrine ordered the dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan.
The Truman Doctrine declared war on the Soviet Union.
